audit.whatIsWrong: Level 1 was 'Skill' while whys[0] and early both say Kled out-trades you there; Levels 4-5 and Level 6 were 'Skill' while whys[3] says your sustain outlasts his mounted health bar and whys[4] says a landed E kills the dismounted Kled.
audit.why: Packet chart is Kled at Level 1 then Illaoi for every later stage, and 51.6% over 531 games is a lane Illaoi wins after the first level.
audit.corrected: Level 1 -> Kled, Levels 4-5 -> Illaoi, Level 6 -> Illaoi, in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.sequencingCues is 0 — Bear Trap was only 'his engage hook, dodge it', with no cooldown and no timing.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11/10/9/8/7s and the yank only lands after the shackle has held for a short duration, so the hook itself is the cue to move. Jousting is 13/12/11/10/9s and is his real disengage from your tentacle swing. Violent Tendencies is 13/12/11/10/9s.
audit.corrected: Bear Trap's 11s and the delayed yank written into the do's; Jousting's 13s written into what Kled wants.

audit.whatIsWrong: Violent Tendencies' auto-attack reset was never named, and itemization told the reader to buy Executioner's Calling because 'his healing fights your pattern' — Kled has no healing ability.
audit.why: Violent Tendencies grants massive attack speed for four attacks with a bigger fourth hit, and carries the autoReset flag, so his burst starts on an auto wind-up. Nothing in Kled's kit heals; Skaarl's courage bar restores mount health on remount, which Grievous Wounds does not touch. Recommending anti-heal here wastes a component slot in a lane where armour into a four-attack frenzy is the real buy.
audit.corrected: Reset tell written into key interactions and the don'ts; the anti-heal line replaced with armour.

edits.before: His engage hook. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Bear Trap is 11s at rank 1; the yank lands a beat after the hook.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: His four-attack Violent Tendencies frenzy rebuilds Skaarl's courage.

edits.before: Track Kled's Bear Trap on a Rope: His engage hook. Dodge it. When it is down — Slam him in your field.
edits.after: Violent Tendencies opens his burst on an auto reset — step on the wind-up, not the cast, then commit after it.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Skip anti-heal — Kled has no healing; armour beats his frenzy.

edits.before: Use his level-1 Q ranged poke to win the early short trades
edits.after: Joust in and out on its 13s cooldown to dodge the tentacle swing

notes: missingInteractions claims Leap of Faith 'shuts off Kled's Jousting and Chaaaaaaaarge!!!'. That comes from a 'grounding' derived flag on Illaoi's R, but Riot's Leap of Faith text describes only damage and a tentacle per champion hit — no grounding. Per the description-over-flag rule I wrote NO grounding claim. The same bad flag is on Illaoi's kit file and will keep generating this suggestion for every matchup; worth fixing at source. wants.foe[0] and wants.foe[1] were near-duplicates (both the level-1 Q poke); [1] repurposed to Jousting.
